newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish debt/currency market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Swedish debt/currency market closing report.

text.p: Swedish yields tracked German debt to end higher and the crown softened.

Some of the crown weakness was because of foreigners taking profits late on Thursday and the currency stayed at these lower levels on Friday. Dealers said the weakening was temporary and that the positive trend would probably continue.
Yields did not react to June Swedish producer price figures, which showed a fall of 0.1 percent versus market expectations for a rise of 0.3 percent.
"Domestic prices rose and that is what is most relevant when judging inflationary pressure," one analyst said.
Domestic prices rose by 0.1 percent month/month.
The market was focusing on dollar/mark and on Bundesbank because of the German central bank's apparent tolerance of the weak mark.

Six month T-bill rates rose one basis point to 4.30 percent and the ten year bond yield rose six basis points to 6.45 percent. The crown softened to 4.2950 crowns against mark versus 4.2885 crowns on Thursday.
